**Gate**
- `findCaseCollisions` walks every segment of every `git ls-files` path, so it compares folder names and file keys within each parent.
- A script file's key is its name without one script extension (`.d.` forms included), and any other entry's key is its full name.
- A collision is two exact keys that are equal ignoring case.
- That catches #34705's shape (`DeploymentNotice.tsx` / `deploymentNotice.ts`, which a full-name check misses), and also folder versus folder, folder versus module (`Foo.ts` / `foo/`), and a declaration file versus a module.
- It correctly does not fire on `foo.ts` / `foo.tsx` or a module beside its test.
- An empty `git ls-files` exits 2 ("nothing read"), not 0.
- The self-test refuses to exit 0 without reaching its verdict.
- The `whole-tree-population` declaration matches the bare `git ls-files`.

**Nit, not blocking**: the extension match is case-sensitive. `Foo.ts` beside `foo.TS` is one name on a case-insensitive file system, but the two keys come out as `Foo` and `foo.TS` and are not compared. Upper-case script extensions are vanishingly rare, so this is noted only. A one-line close is to also compare full names, or to match the extension with `/i`. It is the area's call.

**Workflow step**
- The new step has the sibling's shape: a unique `id`, `continue-on-error: true`, and `run: pnpm check:module-name-case`.
- The lane verdict step reads `toJSON(steps)` and refuses on any red `outcome`, so `continue-on-error` does not silence it. That is the documented pattern in the header of `lint.yml` (around lines 170–190).
- At this head the CI job `Lint · repo & tooling gates` ran the step: "No two names in one folder differ only in letter case → success".

**Acceptance**
- The deliberate pair goes red: the card's own pair on `f6f5b50a`, as the body measures it.
- The tree after #34762 is clean: CI at this head, which carries `main` with the rename.

**Gates**: 70 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 51 `success`, 19 `skipped`, 0 failed. The first-pass `PR-body guards` red (a missing branch claim) was fixed by claim 6946325378 and re-ran green. The lane reports 65/65 derived gates, and I did not re-run them.

## Contract review

Scope: .github/workflows/lint.yml + scripts/check-module-name-case.mjs, package.json

Read for this record: card #34705 (body and its 3 comments), PR #34812 (body, 3 files, the net diff against the merge-base `07f2861fa0`, which is the head's only parent), the 70 check-runs on the head, and, read but not reviewed, `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` and the tree listings of the head and of `origin/main` `3bbda33b78`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set of the repository, new refusal: a tracked tree holding, in one folder, two entries whose keys are equal ignoring case and differ in case. Right: it is the card's item 2, and it is wider than the card's own sketch on purpose. The card's pair (`DeploymentNotice.tsx`, `deploymentNotice.ts`) shares no full name, so the lower-cased `git ls-files` dedupe the card proposed returns nothing on it; the claim comment 6943846096 said so before the code was written, and the script compares module names instead.
- The widening is not a superset of the card's rule. Two full-name shapes the card's sketch would refuse pass this gate: see S1.
- Public surface: none. No package source, no schema, no exported API, no docs page. The root `package.json` is the private workspace manifest; the one added key is a `check:*` script.
- CI surface: one new always-on gate step in the lane `lint-repo-tooling` (`Lint · repo & tooling gates`), which the required aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates` carries. No new job, no new check context, no change to `needs:` or to `OS_AGGREGATOR_MEMBERS`, no new trigger, no permission change. Right.
- Gate verdicts, read off the check-runs on this head: 70 completed, 51 `success`, 19 `skipped`, none failed. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are all `success`.
- Would a pair on `main` today turn it red: no. The head's tree is `07f2861fa0` plus this diff, and the lane ran the scan over it green. `origin/main` `3bbda33b78` adds five paths since then (three changesets and two test files); each was read against its folder's listing and none has a sibling equal ignoring case. The card's folder on `main` now holds `DeploymentNotice.tsx`, `deploymentNoticeState.ts` and `__tests__`. `main` has not touched any of the three files of this diff, nor the verdict script.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no

No changeset and the `skip-changeset` label: right. The diff publishes nothing: a script under `scripts/`, one script key in the private root manifest, one workflow step. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none` are right for the same reason; no skill or docs page teaches file naming.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags and `open_questions`: the final-head note 6947045001 raises none. The one open item in the thread is L1's note in 6947333166 (the extension match is case-sensitive), left as "the area's call". Answered here: it is one of the two shapes of S1, and it is graded there.
- Tier: the lane and L1 both read the step as Tier H under the workflows split because it adds a `continue-on-error`. Agreed; the correction 6947362331 (a contract review is owed on the governed path) is also right, and this record is that review.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff reads `git ls-files` and nothing else; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

Security-touching: no
The step runs a repository script under the lane's existing `contents: read` permission; it adds no secret, no token use, no third-party action, no trigger and no permission.

### ④ Design judgment

**`.github/workflows/lint.yml` (hit).** The change holds against the code it relies on.

- Can the step be green while the script fails: no. `pnpm check:module-name-case` is `--self-test` then the scan joined by a logical and, so either failing exits non-zero (the scan exits 1 on a collision and 2 when `git ls-files` lists nothing; an error thrown by `git` is an uncaught exception). The step's `outcome` is then `failure`.
- Does `continue-on-error` let that red pass the required check: no. `Lane verdict` is the lane's last step, runs under `!cancelled()` and carries no `continue-on-error` of its own. `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` builds its roster from the workflow file, every step of the job that sets `continue-on-error`, so the new step is in it without another edit. It reads each roster step's `outcome` from `toJSON(steps)`, never the `conclusion`. `failure` and `cancelled` are red; a step with no `id:`, or with no outcome in the context, is unread and red; `skipped` is red here too, because the step has no `if:` of its own. Any of these exits 1, the lane concludes `failure`, and the aggregate's `Verify every lint lane succeeded` fails on any `needs` result other than `success`, under `always()`. So the required context `Lint & Repo Gates` goes red.
- The step has the shape the file's own rule asks for (the EVERY GATE RUNS note): a unique `id:` (one occurrence in the file) and `continue-on-error: true`, placed beside its nearest sibling, with the rationale delegated to the script header as the two steps above it do.
- Events and paths: the step has no `if:` and the lane has no paths filter; the lane's only condition is the schedule gate. So the step runs on `push` to `main`, `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `workflow_dispatch`, and on `schedule` unless a green push run already covered the commit, exactly as its neighbours. On `pull_request` and `merge_group` the checkout is the merged tree, so a pair split between the PR and `main` is seen before it lands.
- The lane's checkout precedes the step, so `git ls-files` has an index to read; `Setup workspace` precedes it, so `pnpm` is there.

**`scripts/check-module-name-case.mjs` and the `package.json` key (implementing).**

Agrees with the contract:

- The card's pair collides: `moduleKey` gives `DeploymentNotice` and `deploymentNotice`, equal lower-cased, different exact; the self-test pins that pair and pins that the merged rename (`deploymentNoticeState.ts`) does not collide. The lane measured exit 1 on the tree before #34762 and CI measured exit 0 on the head.
- Folders differing only in case are caught one level up: every path segment is added under its parent, so `Docs/` and `docs/` collide in the root. Index files are covered by the folder key: `Foo.ts` beside `foo/index.ts` collides, and `Index.ts` beside `index.tsx` collides by key.
- Same-case neighbours do not collide (`foo.ts` and `foo.tsx`; a module and its `.test` file), which matches the header's stated exclusion.
- The header's extension list equals `SCRIPT_EXTENSION`. An empty listing is exit 2, not a pass. The self-test sets its verdict flag only after printing a verdict line, and the dispatch refuses when it is unset. The population comment (`whole-tree-population`) matches the bare `git ls-files -z`; `-z` keeps unusual path bytes whole. `ui/` is an ordinary tree at the head, not a gitlink, so its paths are in the population as the header says.

Does not agree:

S1 (should-fix) — the gate passes two shapes of full names that differ only in letter case, which the card's item 2 forbids and which the gate's own words deny. `findCaseCollisions` compares KEYS only, and a full name is never compared when its key differs from its neighbour's by more than case. (a) A folder against a file: `moduleKey` returns a folder's whole name and strips a file's extension, so the folder `Foo.ts/` beside the file `foo.ts` gives keys `Foo.ts` and `foo`, and no collision is reported. On a case-insensitive file system those two are one name and the checkout cannot hold both. (b) An extension that differs in case: `SCRIPT_EXTENSION` is case-sensitive, so `Foo.ts` beside `foo.TS` gives keys `Foo` and `foo.TS`; `Foo.d.ts` beside `foo.D.ts` likewise. This is the shape L1 named. In both the scan exits 0 and prints "no two names in one folder differ only in letter case", the step name says the same, and the header's first line promises "no two tracked names that a case-insensitive file system cannot tell apart" and, under Population, that "a collision anywhere breaks a checkout". The card's sketch (dedupe the lower-cased `git ls-files`) refuses both shapes, so on them the gate is narrower than the rule it implements. Neither shape exists in the tree today: the head lists no script extension with an upper-case letter and no folder whose name ends in a script extension, which is why this is not graded higher. The close is small: compare each entry's full name ignoring case as well as its key, in a key space of its own so a stripped key is never matched against a full name, and add one self-test case per shape. That is a change to the implementing script, so the head moves and the fix is owed a delta review.

N1 (nit) — letter case is folded with `toLowerCase()`, which is not the folding APFS or NTFS apply, and those file systems also treat two Unicode normalisations of one name as equal. Names outside ASCII that collide only under those rules are outside the card and outside this gate. Left as an accepted deviation; no change asked.

Independently, the listing of `origin/main` `c513d62acd` (26,024 files plus their folders) holds no two paths equal ignoring case, which is exactly the full-name space (two full names colliding in a folder make two whole paths equal ignoring case up to that segment, folders included); it holds no script extension with an upper-case letter and no folder whose name ends in a script extension. The module-name space read over the same listing also finds no pair. `main` adds seven paths the head does not have (four changesets and three test files) and lacks only the gate script; none of the seven has a sibling equal ignoring case. - Dev flags and `open_questions`: the final-head note 6947996810 raises none. It asks for this delta on S1 and leaves N1 as recorded; both are answered in ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**`.github/workflows/lint.yml` (hit).** The workflow step's verdict path is unchanged: `lint.yml` did not move in the delta and `main` has not touched it, `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` or `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` since the merge-base, so the prior record's reading holds as written (a red step outcome fails `Lane verdict`, and the required `Lint & Repo Gates` with it). The `package.json` key is unchanged too: self-test, then the scan, joined by a logical and.

**`scripts/check-module-name-case.mjs` (implementing).** The code now agrees with the header, the step name and the card's item 2.

- Both shapes of S1 are caught. Every entry is put twice per folder: under `module` with `moduleKey(name, isFolder)` and under `full` with the bare name. (a) Folder `Foo.ts/` beside file `foo.ts`: full names `Foo.ts` and `foo.ts`, equal lower-cased, two exact keys, one row. (b) `Foo.ts` beside `foo.TS`, and `Foo.d.ts` beside `foo.D.ts`: the module keys still differ by more than case (`Foo` against `foo.TS`; `Foo` against `foo.D`), and the full names collide. The header gained a paragraph stating the rule, so the first line's promise (names a case-insensitive file system cannot tell apart) is now what the code does for ASCII names.
- The separate key space holds. The group key is the space name, a NUL, then the folder; a path segment cannot contain a NUL and the two space names differ, so a `module` group and a `full` group are never the same map, and the folder is recovered by cutting at the first NUL. A stripped key is therefore never compared with a full name. Checked on the brief's two cases: a folder `foo/` beside `foo.ts` gives one exact module key (`foo` twice) and two unrelated full names, so no row; a folder `foo/` beside `Foo.ts` gives no full-name row, and its one row comes from the module space, as on the previous head, which is the header's stated folder-import rule and is pinned by an older self-test. Within the full space there is no false positive at all: two different exact names equal ignoring case in one folder are one name on those file systems, and a folder repeated across many paths is a single exact key. How a non-script file is keyed in the module space (its full name) is the previous head's behaviour, untouched.
- The de-duplication does not drop a distinct collision. First, rows are keyed by folder plus the sorted entry list, so the same pair found by both spaces is one row; entries carry the trailing slash for a folder, so a folder and a file never merge. Second, a row is dropped only when another row of the SAME folder has strictly more entries and names every one of its entries. Every name of a dropped row is still printed on the surviving line, strict length means two rows cannot drop each other, and so at least one row survives whenever any existed: the exit code is never turned from 1 to 0. Rows that overlap without containment both stay (`Foo.ts`, `foo.TS`, `foo.tsx` in one folder print two lines sharing `Foo.ts`), which is right, they are two different pairs.
- The four new self-test cases pin the two shapes. `an extension that differs in case` and `a folder against a file of the same full name` assert the exact row; the `.d.` case asserts one row. Read against the previous head's function, each of the three returns no row there, so each fails without the change. The containment rule is pinned by the older `three spellings are one row` case, which would now be two rows without it.
